title: Skip null elements and count what was consumed

blocks.text: A consumer that calls a method on its input throws `NullPointerException` the moment a list hands it a `null`. A small wrapper keeps that concern apart from the business logic.

items: `nullSafe(Consumer<T> downstream)` returns a consumer that passes non-null inputs to `downstream` and silently ignores `null`.

`forEachCounting(List<T> items, Consumer<T> action)` runs `action` on every non-null item, in order, and returns how many items it ran on. With `forEach`, note that a lambda cannot change a local `int`, so the count lives in something whose reference stays fixed.

blocks.text: Lists may contain `null` and may repeat an item; the count is the number of times the action ran, so a repeated item counts every time.

cases.says: Each item reaches the action once and the count says how many did.
A null element is skipped, so an action that calls a method on it does not throw.
The count covers only the items that reached the action, not the skipped nulls.
An item that appears twice is handed to the action twice and counted twice.

concepts: A counter updated inside a lambda lives in a one-element array or an AtomicInteger.
A consumer without a null check throws on a null element, so a null-safe wrapper skips nulls.
